# 2 Chronicles Chapter 33 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem.

**2** He did evil in the LORD's eyes, following the detestable practices of the nations the LORD had driven out before the Israelites.

**3** He rebuilt the high places his father Hezekiah had demolished, erected altars to the Baals, set up Asherah poles, and worshiped and served all the stars of heaven.

**4** He built pagan altars in the LORD's temple, the place where the LORD had said, "My name will remain in Jerusalem forever."

**5** He built altars to all the stars of heaven in both courtyards of the LORD's temple.

**6** He sacrificed his own children in the fire in the Valley of Ben Hinnom, practiced sorcery and divination, consulted mediums and spiritists. He did enormous evil in the LORD's sight, provoking Him to anger.

**7** He placed a carved idol in God's temple — the very place about which God had told David and Solomon, "In this temple and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I will put My name forever.

**8** I will never again remove Israel from the land I assigned to their ancestors — if only they will be careful to obey everything I commanded them through Moses: the whole law, the decrees, and the regulations."

**9** But Manasseh led Judah and Jerusalem astray, so that they did worse things than the nations the LORD had destroyed before the Israelites.

**10** The LORD spoke to Manasseh and his people, but they ignored Him.

**11** So the LORD brought the army commanders of the king of Assyria against them. They captured Manasseh, put a hook in his nose, bound him with bronze shackles, and took him to Babylon.

**12** In his distress he sought the favor of the LORD his God and humbled himself deeply before the God of his ancestors.

**13** He prayed, and God was moved by his plea. God heard his prayer and brought him back to Jerusalem and to his kingdom. Then Manasseh knew that the LORD is God.

**14** After that, he rebuilt the outer wall of the City of David, west of the Gihon spring in the valley, extending to the entrance of the Fish Gate and encircling the hill of Ophel. He raised it to a great height. He also stationed military commanders in all the fortified cities of Judah.

**15** He removed the foreign gods and the idol from the LORD's temple, along with all the altars he had built on the temple mount and in Jerusalem, and threw them out of the city.

**16** He restored the altar of the LORD and sacrificed fellowship offerings and thank offerings on it. He told Judah to serve the LORD, the God of Israel.

**17** The people, however, continued to sacrifice at the high places, though only to the LORD their God.

**18** The other events of Manasseh's reign, including his prayer to God and the messages the seers spoke to him in the name of the LORD, the God of Israel, are recorded in the annals of the kings of Israel.

**19** His prayer and how God responded to it, and all his sins and unfaithfulness, and the sites where he built high places and set up Asherah poles and idols before he humbled himself — all this is recorded in the records of the seers.

**20** Manasseh rested with his ancestors and was buried in his own palace. His son Amon succeeded him.

**21** Amon was twenty-two when he became king, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem.

**22** He did evil in the LORD's eyes, just as his father Manasseh had done. He worshiped and offered sacrifices to all the idols Manasseh had made.

**23** But unlike his father Manasseh, he did not humble himself before the LORD. Instead, Amon piled up more and more guilt.

**24** His officials conspired against him and assassinated him in his palace.

**25** Then the people of the land killed all who had plotted against King Amon, and they made his son Josiah king in his place.


---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **33:12-13**: The worst king in Judah's history — child sacrificer, idol worshiper, temple defiler — repents in a Babylonian prison, and God takes him back. This is the most radical act of divine mercy in the entire Old Testament. If God can forgive Manasseh, He can forgive anyone.

- **33:13**: "Then Manasseh knew that the LORD is God" — sometimes the only road to this knowledge runs through a Babylonian prison. God's methods are not gentle, but they are effective.

- **33:23**: Amon copies his father's sins but not his father's repentance. The Chronicler's verdict: the difference between Manasseh and Amon is not the depth of their sin but the presence or absence of humility.


— PNEUMA
